item.title: Dutch rights group COC wins Pride Award for 80 years of work
item.description:
Dutch rights group COC wins Pride Award for 80 years of work

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch campaign group COC Nederland, the oldest surviving LGBTQI+ rights organisation in the world, has won the International Pride Award at the WorldPride Human Rights Conference in Amsterdam.

The awards, a joint initiative of the United Nations Development Programme and ILGA World, were presented to five “equality champions” at a ceremony in the Beurs van Berlage on Wednesday. Amsterdam is hosting WorldPride, the global LGBTQI+ event, for the first time this year.

The COC, founded in 1946, was recognised in particular for its support for people in countries where homosexuality is banned or even punishable by death, director Marie Ricardo, who accepted the prize, told broadcaster NOS.

“We support them with coaching, we help them think about how to bring about change in their own surroundings, and we support them with money,” she said.

Ricardo called the award “a recognition of the work we have been doing for 80 years, and the 40 years we have been supporting movements internationally”.

Other winners include South African deputy minister Mmapaseka Steve Letsike and Ugandan transgender pastor Aggie Dennett Harmon.

item.title: Buying your first Dutch house? Good preparation is key
item.description:
Partner content

Buying your first Dutch house? Good preparation is key

August 6, 2026

One aspect of buying a house in the Netherlands is how incomprehensible the entire process can seem. So how does it work, and how can you make sure you get through it all with as little stress as possible?

Let’s say you’ve started looking at the Dutch property market and are thinking perhaps now is the right time to buy a home. There is a lot to sort out and it can be complicated, so what is the most important thing you can do to get ready for success?

“It’s all down to getting your finances sorted out first,” says ABN Amro mortgage advisor Anwar Abdu.

ABN Amro’s SureStarter service, which is currently free, begins with a meeting between the potential homebuyer and a mortgage advisor to assess their financial situation and the size of a possible loan.

“It’s not definitive, but it does give you a very clear indication of what you can borrow,” says Anwar. “That means you can start house hunting. When you’ve found a house that meets your wishes, then you can place a bid, either by yourself or through a buying agent, and you know the maximum amount you can offer.”

How much can you bid?
Overbidding remains very much the norm in the overheated Dutch housing market. According to estate agents’ organisation NVM, in the first quarter of this year, two-thirds of potential buyers offered more than the asking price for a property.

Your estate agent will be able to help you assess how much you should bid, and Anwar does recommend commissioning an agent to help you, especially if you are new to the market. They will take into account the amount of work which needs to be done to the property, the state of the foundations, and general market conditions in the neighbourhood where you are looking to buy.

Together you make an offer on the property and wait to hear if it has been accepted or not. Once a bid has been accepted, the next phase in the process begins: drawing up the purchase agreement. That takes a little time, which can be stressful, but if you checked everything out carefully with your mortgage advisor before you started, there should be no reason to worry.

Get an official valuation
While the purchase agreement is being drawn up, you will need to organise an official valuation of the property so you are ready to move as soon as you have signed the contract. After that, you have a cooling-off period of three days to finalise the mortgage paperwork. A service like SureStarter takes the pressure off by giving you clarity on your financing within those three days.

“So if you sign, say on Monday, you have until midnight on Thursday to finalise your mortgage,” says Anwar. “We’ll fast-track your documents, check your income and complete the paperwork.”

Of course, if you’ve already started the SureStarter process with a mortgage advisor, you’ll have a very good idea about how much you can spend, taking your savings into account, and will have kept within your limits. So that makes it all the more likely you will be able to get the mortgage you need.

Buying a home in the Netherlands can be challenging, but not impossible. With ABN Amro SureStarter, you will know exactly where you stand within three days after signing your purchase contract. Ask for the terms and conditions.

item.title: Dutch state close to breaking even on ABN Amro bailout
item.description:
Dutch state close to breaking even on ABN Amro bailout

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Dutch state is close to recouping the full cost of the 2008 nationalisation of ABN Amro, after a share price rally took the bank’s stock above €40 this week, according to calculations by the Financieele Dagblad.

The finance ministry had long assumed the rescue would be a loss-making operation. In late 2023 it told MPs it was “not realistic” that the state would break even in the short term, projecting a shortfall of almost €7 billion.

Since then the shares have tripled in value, from €13.20 at the time to just over €40 on Thursday. The state, which still owns 20.5% of the bank has now recouped €14.2 billion through staged sell-offs, and its remaining stake is worth some €6.7 billion, the FD said.

That brings the total close to the €21.7 billion the ministry says has been pumped into the bank since 2008.

Slow sell-off
The state bought ABN Amro, Fortis Bank Nederland and the insurer now known as ASR in October 2008 for €16.8 billion to stop parent company Fortis collapsing in the credit crisis, and injected roughly €8 billion more into the banks in the years that followed.

ABN Amro returned to the stock market in 2015, but the share price languished for years and the sell-off repeatedly stalled. Former D66 finance minister Sigrid Kaag restarted the sales in 2023, and every tranche since has fetched a higher price.

Interest paid on the money borrowed for the rescue has been roughly cancelled out by dividend income over the years, the FD said.

Cost cutting
Morningstar analyst Johann Scholtz told the FD the share price rise is partly due to the state selling its stakes and the bank therefore having more freedom to cut costs, along with investors speculating about takeovers in the European banking sector.

The windfall will not plug the cabinet’s budget gaps, however, as one-off share sales cannot be counted towards the deficit under EU rules.

item.title: Jetten thanks firefighters on visit to site of Limburg wildfire
item.description:
Jetten thanks firefighters on visit to site of Limburg wildfire

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Prime minister Rob Jetten has visited the site of a wildfire that has been raging in Limburg for four days, destroying around a square kilometre of woodland.

Jetten thanked emergency workers for their efforts to contain the blaze in the Boshuizerbergen, in a social media video showing “the huge damage to nature and to the animals and people who have had to be evacuated”.

An emergency order banning people from the area remains in force, but limited train services resumed between Venray and Boxmeer on Thursday morning. Arriva had to lay on buses for commuters after the line through the fire zone was closed.

Firefighters said on Wednesday they had brought the blaze under control, only for it to flare up again twice during the night.

Chinook helicopters dropped 900,000 litres of water on the fire in the first two days, drawing it from the Maas in giant buckets containing 7,600 litres.

Efforts to contain the fire have been complicated by the fact that the area contains unexploded Second World War munitions, which bomb disposal specialists have had to make safe.

“In the next few days the fire service and [nature management service] Limburgs Landschap will focus on completely putting out the last sources of the fire. After that we can make a plan to restore this area,” Jetten said.

“I want to thank in particular everyone who has worked so hard in the last few days to deal with this crisis.”

item.title: Vollering closes in on Tour de France lead with stage five win
item.description:
Vollering closes in on Tour de France lead with stage five win

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Demi Vollering closed the gap on Tour de France leader Marlen Reusser to just 12 seconds as she edged out her rivals to claim victory in the fifth stage.

Vollering broke away on the final climb of the 140km stage from Mâcon to Belleville-en-Beaujolais before crossing the line just ahead of Reusser and Kasia Niewiadoma.

Reusser, who took the overall lead in Wednesday’s individual time trial, retained the leader’s yellow jersey, but Vollering reduced the Swiss rider’s lead by claiming the bonus seconds for the stage win.

The trio are the only realistic contenders left for the title after the other hopefuls, including defending champion  Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, who lost two and a half minutes on the day and is back in 17th place, five minutes behind Reusser.

Dutch veteran Anna van der Breggen’s hopes of adding a Tour de France Femmes win to her four Giro d’Italia titles also appear to have been dashed after she crossed the line with Ferrand-Prévot to drop back to 12th place with a deficit of just over four minutes.

The next placed Dutch rider is Femke de Vries, Ferrand-Prévot’s team-mate at Visma Lease-a-Bike, in eighth place, 3 minutes 11 seconds back.

It is the fourth stage victory for 29-year-old Vollering in the women’s tour, which has only existed as a separate race since last year. In 2023 she won the mountain stage to Tourmalet, while the following year she won the time trial in Rotterdam and the climb to the summit of Alpe d’Huez.

“I’m so incredibly proud of this victory,” said the FDJ team leader. “Everyone in the team played their part, which makes it all the sweeter.”

On Thursday the riders will tackle the 153km stage from Montbrison to Tournon-sur-Rhône, with the high point, the 1,099m Col de Lalouvesc, coming at the 105km mark.

item.title: Two explosions at Amsterdam nursery, minors arrested
item.description:
Two explosions at Amsterdam nursery, minors arrested

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have arrested two minors after a second explosive device went off at a children’s nursery in Amsterdam West within a week.

The first blast at the nursery on Bos en Lommerweg happened at around 4am on Saturday morning. The second went off at roughly the same time on Wednesday morning. Nobody was hurt and damage was limited in both cases, broadcaster NOS reported.

Officers detained the two suspects nearby shortly after the second explosion. They are being held under full restrictions, meaning they may only have contact with their lawyers and their parents.

Police said all scenarios are being examined, including whether the two incidents are connected. No motive has been established, broadcaster AT5 reported.

A nursery worker said staff had been badly shaken but that it would stay open as normal.

item.title: Dutch houseboat owners left high and dry by falling river levels
item.description:
Dutch houseboat owners left high and dry by falling river levels

August 6, 2026 Gordon Darroch

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Low water levels in the Rhine delta are causing problems for owners of Dutch houseboats, with no sign of an imminent end to the drought.

Some houseboats and static barges have been standing dry for over a month, resting on platforms that are not designed to support them out of the water or the exposed riverbed.

The Rhine sank to its lowest recorded level last week of 6.46 metres at Lobith, where it enters the Netherlands from Germany, while the flow in the river is one-third of its normal level for July because of low rainfall further upstream.

“We’ve seen these water levels more often in recent years, but usually not until September, and then it gets better after a few days’ rain,” Peter Broekmeulen, board member of the houseboat owners’ association LWO told broadcaster NOS.

The problems for dried-up houseboat owners go further than being stuck above dry land. Several homes have tilted, causing doors and windows to jam and cracks to appear in walls.

Power cables become strained and water pipes crack as they are stretched by the sinking houseboats.

But the biggest challenge is drainage, as residents have had to create improvised systems to deal with waste water that usually flows into the river.

“Open septic tank”

“When the water is there it flows away, but now they’re standing dry it ends up on the land and you get a kind of open septic tank, which is unacceptable from a public health point of view,” Broekmeulen told DutchNews.

Paul van de Veen, who has lived on Rosandepolder in Arnhem, for 40 years, told NOS: “In the early years our boat once had to be towed away by a sailing boat because the water was too high. Now we’re seeing the other side of the coin.”

Van de Veen’s house is still floating after the council dredged his side of the river in February. “We still have a margin,” he said. “The water around us is around a metre deep.”

His neighbours across the water are less fortunate. Marloes Kraal, whose houseboat is in the neighbouring municipality of Renkum, is on a section of river that dried up months ago. “We have cracks in the wall and the roof and there are more appearing,” she said.

The LWO is calling for councils to be more consistent in their policies for houseboats to avoid postcode lotteries arising. Arnhem paid the dredging of the river bank in February from public funds, but in Renkum owners have been told that removing the clay from the riverbed is their own responsibility.

“They are paying the same rent but get much less value for money,” Broekmeulen said. “Legally the council are in the right, but if one council dredges and the other doesn’t, that leads to inequalities.”

Wild west situation

“That’s the wild west situation that we’re up against. We want it to be better regulated nationally for everyone who has to deal with low water levels.”

Owners also face problems when the river levels rise again, as exposed houses can become stuck to their bases, causing them to flood rather than float.

Gert Schols, shipping expert at insurance company EOC, said: “We advise houseboat owners not to go on holiday in periods of extreme drought or arrange a housesitter. You need to keep an eye on what’s happening when the water rises.”

Without action from the government, living on Dutch houseboats risks becoming unappealing in the long term as droughts become more frequent, Broekmeulen warned: “If your house is lying off centre for six months, you’re going to start thinking about moving into one that stands upright.”

item.title: End of a cycling empire? Bike maker Accell at risk of bankruptcy
item.description:
End of a cycling empire? Bike maker Accell at risk of bankruptcy

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Accell, one of the Netherlands’ biggest bicycle groups, has been granted protection from its creditors to hold off the risk of bankruptcy.

The move will give the company court-approved breathing space to try to restructure its debts but leaves its future in doubt.

It is not yet clear how this will impact people with an Accell bike, or for the shops that sell and service them. Neither the company nor the courts have said anything about warranties, spare parts, or outstanding claims from the 2024 recall of tens of thousands of bikes, which were pulled from sale over cracking frames.

Accell owns some of the most well-known names in Dutch cycling – Batavus and Sparta city bikes, Koga touring bikes, and the Babboe and Carqon cargo brands – as well as Raleigh, Lapierre, and the German marques Haibike, Winora, and Ghost. It employs around 3,700 people in 15 countries.

Four difficult years
The company was publicly listed in Amsterdam until private equity group bought it for €1.56 billion in 2022.

It has struggled ever since the covid pandemic. Demand for bikes surged during the pandemic but parts were hard to get, and by the time supply chains recovered Accell was left with a mountain of unsold stock. Revenues fell 22% in 2024 to just over €1 billion.

A series of cutbacks followed: its warehouse network was reduced from 85 sites to 28, its Turkish factory was sold, and its Heerenveen plant closed last spring, ending its bicycle manufacturing in the Netherlands. Production moved to Hungary and France.

Earlier this year Accell struck a deal with its creditors, who took ownership of the company. That was always a stopgap, and a search for a new owner began. Accell said it held talks with several interested parties, assessed a number of bids, and sought regulatory approval for a possible merger, but no workable solution emerged.

item.title: Double Dutch victory blows Canadian Open tennis draw wide open
item.description:
Double Dutch victory blows Canadian Open tennis draw wide open

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The top two Dutch tennis players, Tallon Griekspoor and Botic van de Zandschulp, have both claimed major scalps in the second round of the Canadian Open.

Griekspoor, who turned 30 last month, put a wretched season behind him to knock out the world number three, top seed and French Open champion Alexander Zverev in three sets.

Zverev appeared to have overcome an early wobble when he rescued a set point before taking the first set on a tie-break.

But Griekspoor hit straight back to take a 4-0 lead in the second set, going on to win 6-2, before breaking the German twice in the decider to win 6-4.

“This is one of my most special wins,” Griekspoor said on court after the match. “There were times this year when I almost threw in the towel.”

Van de Zandschulp matched his achievement as he overcame blustery conditions to see off the Russian number four seed, Daniil Medvedev, in straight sets.

Multiple breaks

In an opening set that featured six breaks of serve, the 30-year-old Dutchman prevailed 6-3. The players broke each other twice in the second before Van de Zandschulp won the tie-break 7-5 with a sublime pass on his second match point.

VAN DE ZANDSCHULP MEDVEDEV! #ZiggoSport #ATP1000 #OBN26 pic.twitter.com/pZauCKqfH8

— Ziggo Sport (@ZiggoSport) August 6, 2026

“It was difficult for me and Daniil to play this evening and I’m happy that I got over the line in the end,” Van de Zandschulp said.

The results leave the draw wide open after world number one Jannik Sinner and 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic opted to sit out the tournament, while the number two player Carlos Alcaraz is recovering from a wrist injury.

Griekspoor will face the Italian Matteo Arnaldi, who knocked him out of this year’s French Open, in the round of 32, while Van de Zandschulp takes on Poland’s Hubert Hurkacz.

Both players are also likely to rise in the ATP rankings from their current positions of 69th for Griekspoor and 70th for Van de Zandschulp as a result of their wins.

item.title: Bol and De Bijenkorf warn customers of possible data leak
item.description:
Bol and De Bijenkorf warn customers of possible data leak

August 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Online retailer Bol and department store chain De Bijenkorf have emailed customers to warn that their personal details may have been exposed in a cyberattack on a logistics company both firms use.

Hackers may have gained access to systems at CEVA Logistics, which handles deliveries for both companies. Names, addresses, postcodes, and phone numbers are among the details that may have been taken, broadcaster NOS reported.

Bol said its own systems were not affected and that the incident involves orders from a single distribution centre. Neither company has said how many customers may be affected, and De Bijenkorf has commissioned an external investigation into the breach.

Bol said there is no indication that payment details, passwords, or login credentials were affected and has taken part of its range offline – products handled by the logistics company – cancelled some orders, and stopped exchanging data with the firm as a precaution.

De Bijenkorf blocked access to the systems involved and added further security measures. It says customers may face delays to orders, returns, and refunds, and that email addresses and product information may also have been taken. The chain said it was certain no bank account numbers or passwords had been exposed.

CEVA told Bol about the possible breach on August 1 and the Dutch data protection authority AP was informed on August 3, but customers were only emailed on Wednesday.

A Bol spokesperson told NOS the company wanted to establish first what had happened and who was affected, rather than contacting people repeatedly.
